messages:
maria: Async standup — SLOs / alerting / oncall follow-ups

what I did: triaged 3 high-rate pages overnight, narrowed down to kv-cache eviction spike on a specific shard. Increased warmup jobs on staging and collected eviction histograms.

blockers: still getting noisy paging when prefix churn > 12 req/s; unsure if debounce window should be host-level or alert-type-level.

today: rolling canary for kv-warmup changes (2 nodes), open PR for alert debounce logic — will ask for review. planning a failure-mode sim at 15:30 PT.

---

tj: thanks — can you paste the PR link and current page rate avg? :thumbsup:

maria: PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/842
current pager avg (last 1h): ~4.8/min, but bursts to ~22/min for the affected shard.

---

drew: pinged on review. quick note: tests failing on the time-based TTL mock, I'll fix this morning. lgtm otherwise.

maria: noted, thanks. re: debounce, I prototyped config like:
```
alert:
  name: kv-evict-rate
  threshold: 30
  window_seconds: 60
  debounce_seconds: 300
  scope: host  # alternatives: host, shard, service
```
Would prefer host-level for now.

---

oncall-bot: ALERT (kv-evict-rate) fired for host-r4g-12 — count=48 in 60s — runbook: /runbooks/kv-evict.md

elaine: re SLO impact — these bursts are spiking 99p latency for generation endpoints. Suggest temp suppress during rolling warmup + update runbook to include "check cache fill rate" step.

maria: agreed. @tj can you add a suppression rule scoped to the canary tag? also need quota approval for 2 canary nodes.

tj: I can add the suppression rule and approve quota. assigning runbook update to myself.

---

drew: I'll run the failure sim at 15:30 PT and post logs. will include a small script to hammer prefixes.

maria: blocker resolved — tj approved quota. moving canary to deploy.

tj: added suppression rule (suppression id: sup-202304-77). runbook updated draft in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/19

maria: perfect, thanks everyone. I'll watch canary and mute noisy alerts; will post a short postmortem if we see regressions. :rocket:

elaine: thanks! if the sim shows >5% error increase, escalate to incident channel.

maria: will do.
